# Review (pass 1) — secret-history-278-278 (§278)

Reviewer worked from conventions.md, runbook.md, packet.md, units.json, novel-forms.json, known-forms.json, the pilot model
and the glossary only; no modern translation consulted; English phrases rebuilt from grammar and Ming glosses.
`units.json` edited in place by script (backup of the drafter's file kept outside the repo); `t` never retyped.

Integrity checks after editing (all pass): 92 units, 610 words consumed once in packet order; every unit's `t` equals the
packet words joined by single spaces; every word has exactly one `words` entry; every Ming bracket in every morph gloss equals
the packet's Ming gloss for that word; keys and `p` flags unchanged; schema unchanged.

Unit numbers below are 0-based indexes into `sentences` (U0 = first unit). The drafter's notes cross-refer to units 1-based
(e.g. "unit 30" = U29); I kept that convention in `n` (see refused findings).

Counts: critical 0 · major 3 · moderate 17 · minor 27 (47 entries, numbered below).

## Major

1. **U15 · l, i, n, morph (words 81, 86, 87)** — The drafter read `ekid an-u` as "heads of the night guard" and `an-u` as "his/him", so `i` came out as word-salad ("the heads of the night guard … are to cleave and cut him down"). `an-u` (Ming 他的) is the glossary's "their (third-person genitive placed after its noun)", so `ekid an-u` is "their heads" (those of the people seized). Done: `l` "his" → "their"; `i` rebuilt ("others, people who enter inward by force: the night guard who have seized them are to split and hack their heads, and let it go at that"); `n` gains the an-u explanation and says what "let it go" stands for; `an-u` is now one morph (as in-ü in the model); `ekid` gloss no longer says "beginning" (glossary: eki "brain, head"); `žöričen` now carries the glossary's lemma žöri- with the Ming 交慘 flagged (see moderate list).
2. **U72 · i, n** — `jabuqui-jan` has the reflexive -(i)jan, which points back to the offender, not to "us"; `i` ("it has been a hardship for us, for our going") made the hardship ours and dropped the offender. Done: `i` "he has made it hard for us in his own going about"; `n` explains the reflexive and keeps "our own" as the alternative; "to us, our own going" in `n` → "his own going".
3. **U85 · i** — `Aqalaγdaba keġen` is Ming 彼爲長了 "he was made senior" (and the drafter's own note says so), but `i` had "I have been made senior". Done: "He has been made senior".

## Moderate

4. **U2 · i** — `daγ̇ulγaqui` was rendered as an active participle ("a decree newly proclaiming the rules"), contradicting the note ("to be proclaimed"); "rules" is not in the text. Done: `i` "all the guardsmen's conduct — a decree newly to be proclaimed. In proclaiming it, he said:"; `l` "proclaiming" → "to-be-proclaimed".
5. **U17 · l, i, n, morph 99** — `ümerēče` was glossed "north (?)… from the north / at the north side". The glossary's published reading is ümer "behind, back" + ablative, with the Ming 北處 case rendered "from behind the tent" (ger-ün ümerēče). Done: morph split ümer + -ēče (Ming 北 kept as a bracket note); `l` "from-behind"; `i` "behind the tent"; `n` explains the bracketed 北.
6. **U19 · l, i, n, morph 117** — `žilda` rendered "at night"/"by night"; the glossary reads it "late, evening" from the Ming 晩夕, and the drafter's own gloss said "Ming 晩夕 'evening'". Done: "in the evening" in `l`, `i`, `n`, morph. Also `i` "a man we trust" → "a trusted man" ("we" is not in the text).
7. **U32 · l, i, n, morph 207** — `öġere` (Ming 𠮠) is "apart, separately" in the glossary; the drafter glossed "other, different" and left it out of `i`. Done: morph, `l` "separately", `i` "…not go out separately, apart from us", `n`.
8. **U33 · i** — `čaγlažu talbižu` are converbs that depend on the optative of the next unit; `i` made them a statement ("they will weigh the matter and leave"). Done: "weighing the matter and leaving half…", leading into U34's "and let the other half…".
9. **U77 · i** — `sonosγatuγai` is causative "make hear"; `i` had "have this decree read" ("read" is not in the text). Done: "make the guardsmen hear this decree".
10. **U86 · i** — the conditional of `kürgeġesü` was dropped ("then the answer…"); also "a man" was supplied. Done: "if they lay hand or foot on him, the answer to a fist" (glossary: γar kürge- "to lay a hand on").
11. **U87 · i** — final optative `qariγ̇ultuγai` ("let it be answered", as the note says) was lost. Done: "…is a rod: let it be so answered."
12. **degeġün · morph (words 119, 141, 149; U19, U22, U24)** — split deġe + "-ġün locative", a label stated as fact; the glossary has degeġün as one word ("above, upper side"; ending uncertain). Done: one morph, lemma degeġün.
13. **žaγaγ̇un / žaqaγ̇un · morph (words 145, 151; U23, U24) and U23 · n** — split žaγa "edge" + locative; glossary: žaγaγun "between" (Ming 兩間). Done: one morph, lemma žaγaγun, printed form noted; `n` of U23 corrected.
14. **qoinaγ̇un, uridaγ̇un · morph (words 61, 62; U12)** — "-γ̇un = locative" asserted; glossary: "ending -γ̇un uncertain". Done: "ending of uncertain force, read as a locative".
15. **bi-že · morph (words 131, 589, 598; U20, U88, U89) and `n` of U20, U88** — lemma `bi` "is (perhaps short for bü-)"; glossary: bü- "to be; stem bi- before -že, 'indeed is'". Done: lemma bü-, že as "indeed, so"; U20 `n` and U88 `n` ("let it be so" → "indeed is", matching `i`).
16. **öġesüd · morph (word 570; U85)** — lemma öġe + "-süd plural (uncertain)"; glossary: öġesün + plural -d (the -n drops). Done.
17. **žöričen · morph (word 81; U15)** — a word in the glossary (žöri- "to cross each other's paths", Ming 相錯) given a new lemma; the drafter's sense rests on a different Ming (交慘). Done: lemma žöri- with the glossary sense, the Ming here and the uncertainty stated.
18. **eteġed · morph (words 262, 278, 291, 306, 322, 339; U41, U43, U45, U47, U49, U51)** — "-d = plural" stated flatly while `i` reads a single "side" ("on the left side"); the glossary says "-d may be a plural or part of the stem". Done: the -d is marked uncertain, noting the Ming 邊 is singular.
19. **Quote marks in `l` (U3, U4, U6, U8, U19, U20, U29, U31, U37, U51, U54, U57, U63, U65, U67, U85, U87, U90)** — conventions (230–236): `l` mirrors Shiratori's quote marks (straight), `i` supplies omitted openings. The drafter's `l` had curly closers only, no openers, missed the closers at U4, U19, U20, and put invented single quotes in U85. Done by script: all quote chars stripped from `l`, then straight `"` set exactly where `t` carries them (openers U3, U6, U31, U56, U65, U67; closers U4, U8, U19, U20, U29, U37, U51, U54, U57, U63, U65, U87, U90; mid-unit closers before keġen/keġebe placed on the marked word); U85's invented ‘ ’ removed. `i` quote handling checked and left: every double pair balances (U3–4, U6–8, U10–29, U31–37, U39–51, U52–54, U56–57, U59–63, U65, U67–87, U88–90), inner singles at U19, U20, U81, U85 balance, and the supplied openings are named in `n`.
20. **Names in `l` (U37, U40, U42, U44, U46, U48, U50, U52, U56, U60, U62, U63, U65)** — conventions: Shiratori's form in `l`, plain English only in `i`. The drafter used English respellings in `l` (Qada'an, Bulqadar, Chanar, Qori-Qachar, Jalbaq, Qara'udar, Jesün-Te'e, Bügidei, Qorqudaq, Lablaqa, Alchidai, Küje, Mongqutai, Eljigidei) while using Shiratori's elsewhere (Elžigidei U19, Qoṅγortai U18). Done: all now Shiratori's printed forms (checked against each unit's `t`); `i` untouched and already matches the house spellings.

## Findings refused (with reasons)

- **Commas in `l` that Shiratori does not print** (U11 "Door-at,", U33 "hunting-at,", U32, etc.): the pilot's `l` uses readability commas freely; only quote marks are mirrored by convention. Only the colon at U1 was a misleading mirror and was changed.
- **ejetüldüžü split eje + -tü- + -ldü- + -žü** (8 words): the glossary has ejetüldü- as one stem "analysis uncertain"; the drafter's split is flagged uncertain and keeps the house lemma eje (Ming 商量). Left.
- **-dekü as a participle (üküġüldekü, keseġegdekü)** vs the passive -de- + -kü: the glossary itself has both analyses (mököriġüldekü "participle -dekü"; üküġüldekün "passive -de- + -kün"). Followed the published mököriġüldekü; noted as a doubt.
- **ajaγa "cup, vessel" / "cups and dishes" (U28)**: matches the glossary's published "cup, vessel (Ming 器)". Left.
- **miṅγaloγ̇udai-ji (word 605)**: the morph (plural -γ̇ud + genitive -ai) is the glossary's own tentative analysis; `i` keeps the Ming 千的 singular "the thousand-commander". Internal tension noted as a doubt, not forced either way.
- **min-u as two morphs (bi + -u), U1, U53, U88 …**: the glossary keys min-u whole, but morph entries are per morpheme the reader sees; the model does the same for -(n)u. Left. (an-u, by contrast, followed the model's one-morph in-ü and was changed.)
- **eġüdečin = eġüde + -čin (U36)**: glossary has eġüden + -či + -n; both readings reach "door-keeper" and the label is not misleading. Left.
- **U19 "across the night guard's ground"**: "ground" is supplied (degeġün "above/over", Ming 上經過), like "station" in U22/U24; hedged, tied to the note. Left, listed as a doubt.
- **U54 "take charge of the banquet" for tüsürge barituγai** (bari- "hold"): defensible beside house "barin atuγai 'stay to hold'"; left.
- **U42 `n` sentence "The first nigen kešig here is bolžu 'being'"**: obscure but not wrong. Left.
- **"-(i)jar/-(i)jan … back-vowel form after the linking (i)" wording** (U3 etc.): oddly phrased but conveys that the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel; the glossary's "-(i)jan" entry uses the same device. Left.
- **U2 `n` "from the same root as tuṅγaγ̇a-"**: the note already says the stem is uncertain. Left.
- **Cross-references to units in `n` are 1-based** ("unit 30", "unit 64", "units 42 and 46"): all of them check out in the 1-based count, and are consistent with each other. Not renumbered; if the page shows unit numbers differently the notes will need a pass.
- **`titleEn`/`part` use "§278" (single) where the runbook pattern is "§§A–B"**: no single-section example in the model; the form reads correctly. Left.
- **Bidan-i "accusative on the subject" (U33)**: matches the glossary's bidan-i entry. Left.
- **U13 "converb chain, left whole"**: a loose description of one converb; harmless. Left.

## Remaining doubts

- U14–U15 as a whole (the sense of `busud … oγ̇ortuγai`, and what "let it go" means) remains the weakest unit; `n` says so.
- Whether U19/U20's inner quotations pair as the drafter (and I) read them (Shiratori prints only closers at bariγdalaγ̇a" and bi-že").
- U7 (narataj-a, mör-tür(i)-jen), U57 (aγsaquj-a; "auxiliary" for ačid), and U72 (reflexive reading) are readings, not certainties.
- miṅγaloγ̇udai-ji: plural analysis vs singular rendering.
- Whether `ümerēče` should keep "north" somewhere visible; I kept it only in the morph gloss and note.
- Passive analysis of -dekü (see refused list).
